definition: A training schedule technique that gradually increases the learning rate from a small value at the start of training before transitioning to the main schedule.
details: Learning rate warmup helps stabilize training in the early stages, particularly for large transformer models, where using the full target learning rate immediately can lead to instability or divergence.

explainer.lead: Learning rate warmup gradually increases the learning rate from a small value at the start of training before transitioning to the main schedule. It helps stabilize training in the early stages, particularly for large transformer models.

tiers.eli5: Instead of slamming the accelerator at the start, training eases in gently before settling into its normal pace.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers insert a short ramp-up before the main schedule when training large transformers. Using the full target learning rate immediately risks instability or divergence.
tiers.paperLevel: A training schedule that rises from a small initial learning rate to the main schedule; starting at the full target rate can lead to instability or divergence.

explainer.example: A large transformer begins training with a small learning rate that ramps up, then switches to its main schedule.
